results.reason: Issue 3 flags MSA 12.2. Supplier may assign to any third party without consent or notice, while Customer is restricted. It explains the risk of an assignee that competes with Brightwater and recommends mutual restrictions, consent or notice, and a competitor carve-out.

Issue 2 flags that MSA 10.3 carves Customer's indemnity out of the 10.1 cap, while Supplier's indemnity stays capped. It explains Brightwater's unlimited exposure and recommends capping, narrowing and making the indemnities mutual.

Issue 4 flags the automatic successive 36-month renewals in Order Form 2.2 with 30-day notice. It explains the three-year lock-in and recommends a shorter renewal term, a longer notice window and calendaring the deadline.

Issue 1 flags the consent requirement and Supplier termination right in Order Form 6.1. It ties them to the pending majority equity sale and recommends deleting or softening the clause, or obtaining written consent or waiver before closing.

Issues are ranked, with change of control and the uncapped indemnity marked HIGH. Each entry cites document and section, explains why it matters, and gives a recommended fix.

Addressed to the Supervising Partner with a bottom line that Brightwater should not sign as drafted. It includes a cross-document alignment section noting that Exhibit A raises no issue, plus client-call talking points.
